claims.text: The baseline TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC alloy with a dendritic microstructure.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a low-temperature yield strength of about 800 MPa.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The baseline TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of 423 MPa at 1273 K and 30% strain.
Mechanical alloying and consolidation with 1-3 vol% Y2O3 or TiC nanoparticles will produce a fine nanoparticle dispersion in the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
Y2O3 or TiC nanoparticles will remain thermally stable under the proposed elevated-temperature conditions.
The nanoparticle dispersion will pin dislocations in the TiVNbTa matrix.
The nanoparticle dispersion will pin grain boundaries in the TiVNbTa matrix.
Orowan strengthening from the nanoparticles will impede dislocation motion at elevated temperature.
Zener pinning by the nanoparticles will suppress grain growth at elevated temperature.
Impeded dislocation motion and suppressed grain growth will improve retention of strength at 1273 K.
The nanoparticle-modified alloy will achieve at least a 30% increase in yield strength at 1273 K relative to the baseline.
The nanoparticle-modified alloy will have a yield strength greater than 430 MPa at 1273 K.
The nanoparticle-modified alloy will achieve at least a 30% increase in compressive strength at 1273 K and 30% strain relative to the baseline.
The nanoparticle-modified alloy will have a compressive strength greater than 550 MPa at 1273 K and 30% strain.
The nanoparticle-modified alloy will exhibit improved microstructural stability during testing and thermal cycling between room temperature and 1273 K.
Nanoparticle agglomeration or reaction would invalidate the proposed strengthening regime.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on nanoparticle distribution and stability.
The direction of the predicted strength change is supported by prior evidence.
